H_hierarchical.evidence: The secondary controller has efficiency/thermal/resonance mode grouping, but S1-S4 are flat inverter-count states with no parent-child FSM.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Temperature, load, and harmonic triggers use threshold comparisons plus OR aggregate indicators T, δ, and H over per-inverter variables.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions switch Boolean status variables, activate/deactivate inverters, redistribute load, and update inverter power-reference commands.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: No emergency stop, rollback, abort-from-any-state, or explicit fault-recovery transition is specified.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: S1-S4 and the truth table are defined in the islanded secondary-control subsection, while THD-triggered shifting and power-reference updates appear later in the grid-connected resonance subsection.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as active thermal management, efficiency optimization, operating point A/B, and resonance mitigation require mapping domain intent to inverter-count transitions.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The θ truth table gives state meanings, while actions such as sequential activation, inverter-count reduction, and power-reference update are described in prose/equations.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: Aggregate guards include T=T1∨..., δ=δ1∨..., and H=H1∨..., combined with Te>Tc, Px<50%Prated, and HM>Hc thresholds.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite state has its own entry, during, or exit behavior beyond substates.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The paper does not declare a from-any-state fault or safe-state escape rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is no deep composite state or non-trivial init/pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Three guard families combine threshold comparisons with Boolean aggregation across inverter variables.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Global secondary-control indicators T, δ, and H drive shifts among S1-S4, but the paper does not state an explicit from-any-state forced transition.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are concrete inverter enable/status bits and power-reference commands, not abstract log/publish/notify actions.

each state can be shifted by a Boolean condition
one_line_pitch: A flat but guard-heavy microgrid supervisor forces recovery of threshold/OR transition logic and action semantics spread across thermal, efficiency, and harmonic-control prose.
rationale: The sample is a real FSM benchmark item because the paper explicitly defines S1-S4, inverter on/off semantics, Boolean threshold guards, and meaningful inverter-count and power-reference actions. It is baseline-difficult because the state table, guard definitions, thermal/efficiency behavior, and harmonic-resonance action are distributed across the control-architecture narrative rather than one compact specification. It is backup rather than candidate because hierarchy is only superficial mode grouping and there is no fault-recovery or global escape pattern.
